original_question: Kropholler’s hierarchy(see 15.45) is closed under finite extensions, that is, (Hα F)F ⊆ Hα F for every α (P. Kropholler, J. Pure Appl. Algebra, 90(1993), 55–67). Let a hierarchy of tdlc groups HK be defined analogously to Kropholler’s hierarchy in 15.45, with K being the class of profinite groups and with the cell stabilisers of the admissible action required to be open. Is it true that HK is closed under profinite extensions, that is, (Hα K)K ⊆ Hα K for every α?
target_in_paper: Problem 21.36 in the section "New Problems (21st issue, 2026)": the tdlc analogue of Kropholler's hierarchy and whether each stage is closed under profinite extensions.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact target almost verbatim. It correctly identifies the relevant discrete antecedent from 15.45, correctly states the finite-extension closure for Kropholler's hierarchy, correctly switches from the class F of finite groups to the class K of profinite groups, correctly imposes openness of cell stabilisers in the tdlc setting, and correctly asks whether (H_αK)K is contained in H_αK for every ordinal α.
missing_details: The draft is not fully stand-alone because it relies on 15.45 for the definition of the hierarchy: for a class X, H_1X consists of groups admitting an admissible action on a finite-dimensional contractible complex with all cell stabilisers in X.
It does not explicitly unpack the transfinite hierarchy H_αK; to make the question self-contained one should specify the successor-step and limit-step construction.
It assumes the reader knows that the ambient objects are totally disconnected, locally compact groups.
It does not explicitly say that K denotes the class of all profinite groups.
It leaves the class-product notation (H_αK)K implicit; to be fully stand-alone, one should say that this means tdlc groups G having a closed normal subgroup N in H_αK with profinite quotient G/N.

It inherits the paper's use of the term "admissible action" without definition; a stand-alone version should either retain it as part of the quoted setup from 15.45 or restate the setup from that problem.
refined_question: Let K be the class of profinite groups, and define a transfinite hierarchy {H_αK} of totally disconnected, locally compact groups analogously to Kropholler's hierarchy from Problem 15.45: H_1K consists of those tdlc groups that admit an admissible action on a finite-dimensional contractible complex whose cell stabilisers are open and belong to K; for successor ordinals, H_{α+1}K := H_1(H_αK); and for limit ordinals λ, H_λK := ⋃_{β<λ} H_βK. Is it true that every stage H_αK is closed under profinite extensions, i.e. for every ordinal α does (H_αK)K ⊆ H_αK hold, where (H_αK)K denotes the class of tdlc groups G with a closed normal subgroup N ∈ H_αK such that G/N is profinite?
justification: The exact official target is Problem 21.36, and your draft is already essentially its wording. The only paper-faithful refinement needed is to make explicit the notation imported from 15.45: the definition of H_1X via admissible actions on finite-dimensional contractible complexes, the transfinite stages H_αX, and the fact that in the tdlc analogue the cell stabilisers are required to be open. Since the paper does not broaden this into a more general problem, the refined question should remain exactly about the inclusion (H_αK)K ⊆ H_αK for all ordinals α.
